answer: Sonnet-pace admission gating: each identity must sustain a minimum inter-action delay distribution across its first N actions, checked against a per-window timing envelope. A zephyr of bursty registrations fails the envelope, since cloned agents cannot fake slow, jittered pacing without idling real compute. Attacker cost: N × delay per identity, plus parallel workers to keep pacing, scaling linearly with sybil count. A nebula of slow identities still pays wall-clock time and worker overhead before any action counts.
